jp_verse:
霧の橋

    静かに渡る

    朝の道
en_verse: A bridge in mist\ncrossed without hurry\ninto the morning

jp_verse:
雅の袖

    言葉より先に

    風が舞う
en_verse: Elegant sleeves\nbefore words are spoken\nthe wind already speaks

jp_verse:
空の下

    ただ立つだけで

    道となる
en_verse: Beneath the sky\nsimply standing still\nbecomes a path

jp_verse:
雨の灯

    声にならない

    夜が落ちる
en_verse: Rain and lanterns\na voice that cannot form\nfalls into night

jp_verse:
紙重ね

    静かな時を

    綴じてゆく
en_verse: Layered papers\nbinding together\nquiet moments of time

jp_verse:
旗揺れて

    争わぬまま

    風競う
en_verse: Banners trembling\nwithout open conflict\nthe winds compete

jp_verse:
空高く

    誰も触れえぬ

    古き座
en_verse: High beneath heaven\nan ancient throne\nnone may reach

jp_verse:
香の煙

    執着だけが

    遠ざかる
en_verse: Incense drifting\nonly attachment\nmoves farther away

jp_verse:
泥の道

    小さな歌を

    口ずさむ
en_verse: Along muddy roads\na small child quietly\nhums to himself

jp_verse:
空映す

    静かな瞳に

    雲流る
en_verse: The sky reflected\ninside a quiet pupil\nclouds continue on

jp_verse:
夕の鐘

    山の霧へと

    響き消ゆ
en_verse: An evening bell\nechoing outward\ninto mountain mist

jp_verse:
灯の市

    人と人とを

    結びゆく
en_verse: Lantern market\nbinding person to person\nthrough exchange

jp_verse:
深き袖

    家を静かに

    受け継ぎぬ
en_verse: Within layered robes\nthe house is quietly\ncarried onward

jp_verse:
石の庭

    乱れぬ道に

    風も合う
en_verse: Stone garden paths\neven the passing wind\nmoves in harmony

jp_verse:
雨しずく

    古き屋根より

    時落ちる
en_verse: Raindrops falling\nfrom the ancient temple roof\ntime itself descends

jp_verse:
見えぬ影

    遠き静けさ

    刃は抜かず
en_verse: An unseen shadow\nwithin distant stillness\nno blade is drawn

jp_verse:
茶の湯気に

    静かな木匙

    夜ぬくむ
en_verse: In rising tea steam\na quiet wooden spoon\nwarms the evening

jp_verse:
厳しさも

    愛の形と

    子は知らず
en_verse: Even stern words\nare sometimes the shape\nof love unseen

jp_verse:
花ひらき

    名もなき記憶

    風に立つ
en_verse: Flowers opening\nnameless memories rise\nupon the wind

jp_verse:
日が傾き

    語らぬものが

    空に残る
en_verse: As daylight fades\nthe unspoken things remain\nwithin the sky
